framing.lineOfInquiry: Yogesh Malhotra (P00138) may have been involved in the incident recorded in CASE027
framing.alternate: Yogesh Malhotra (P00138) was not involved — the evidence has an innocent explanation
framing.note: KRONOS starts from the presumption of innocence. The line of inquiry and the alternates are tested against the same records; neither is a finding, and the strengths are not probabilities.

alternateHypotheses.title: Was near the scene for a routine reason
alternateHypotheses.statement: Yogesh Malhotra was near the scene because they regularly go there (home, work, market), not because of the incident.
alternateHypotheses.label: Moderate

evidence.text: Recorded within 1 km of the scene on 40 other days (27 Mar – 24 May), so presence there is part of their routine

alternateHypotheses.test: Establish why the person is regularly there (address, employment, shop) and compare the incident-time visit with their usual pattern (time of day, duration).

alternateHypotheses.title: The location records are unreliable
alternateHypotheses.statement: Yogesh Malhotra's location records are imprecise or inconsistent (tower-level accuracy, cloned or shared SIM), so they do not reliably place them at the scene.
alternateHypotheses.label: Moderate

evidence.text: The record placing them near the scene (CDR) is only accurate to about 1.5 km

alternateHypotheses.test: Request a tower dump and the handset's GPS logs; check for SIM cloning; rely on high-accuracy fixes only.

alternateHypotheses.title: Named or given a role in error
alternateHypotheses.statement: Yogesh Malhotra was named in the FIR, or assigned a role, without an independent basis.
alternateHypotheses.label: Moderate
alternateHypotheses.test: Re-examine the FIR and statements; record the person's statement and the informant's basis for naming them.

alternateHypotheses.title: The contact was routine, not coordination
alternateHypotheses.statement: Yogesh Malhotra's calls and messages reflect a long-standing relationship (family, work, business), not planning of the incident.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: In contact with Aarti Saini since 2025-03-28, 28 days before the incident (3 calls, 4 messages) — a long-standing relationship
In contact with Amit Aggarwal since 2025-03-29, 26 days before the incident (10 calls, 7 messages) — a long-standing relationship
In contact with Pankaj Singh since 2025-04-01, 24 days before the incident (4 calls, 3 messages) — a long-standing relationship
Contact around the incident (14) is close to the normal baseline (≈17.8), with no unusual spike

alternateHypotheses.test: Examine message content and the timing of contact relative to the incident; establish the relationship.

alternatesConsideredNotSupported.title: Someone else used the phone or handset
The money has a legitimate explanation

comparison.verdict: Every supporting item could be explained by at least one alternate, although the line of inquiry is stronger on weight (0.75 vs 0.58). Test the alternates before relying on it.
settleWith: A2 — Establish why the person is regularly there (address, employment, shop) and compare the incident-time visit with their usual pattern (time of day, duration).
A8 — Request a tower dump and the handset's GPS logs; check for SIM cloning; rely on high-accuracy fixes only.
A6 — Re-examine the FIR and statements; record the person's statement and the informant's basis for naming them.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Yogesh Malhotra (P00138) was involved in the incident recorded in CASE027
hypotheses.name: Yogesh Malhotra

supporting.text: record within 0.21 km of the incident location within 2 h of the incident

alternativeExplanations: Being named in an FIR records an allegation; it is not itself proof of involvement.
Being near the incident place may be routine (home, work, market) — check whether the person regularly visits it.
verificationSteps: [MEDIUM · value 0.53] Collect CCTV from Ghumar Mandi Market, Ludhiana for 25 Apr 2025 10:27–12:27 (check retention period — footage may already be overwritten) (TO_BE_OBTAINED)

confidence.note: Evidential balance compares weighted supporting vs contradicting evidence; it is not a probability of guilt. Prior records are excluded from this score.

note: Each hypothesis is tested from both sides to reduce confirmation bias. Confidence scores are evidential balance (not probability of guilt). Human review is required.
